about: The regression set of first-person scenes (research/69 "Auditing scenes by rule"): one of each kind (a scripted walk with someone beside Shepard is played walking along, `before`: it waits for a player who stands still), from the validation saves on the owner's machine (tools/save-dictionary.py; %LOCALAPPDATA%\MEVR). Run with tools/conversation-audit.ps1; compared with tools/conversation-audit-baseline.json.
handsAbout: Every scene is played with tracked hands (a recording's, replayed with its inputs: tools/make-walk-recording.py --plan ... --hands view): the fake headset has none, and without them arm IK and the body follower never run (research/69 "The body that stayed at the mark"). They are held up in front of the eyes, so every eye snapshot shows Shepard's drawn hands where the controllers are (research/69 "Seeing the body in the audit"). A scene's own `hands` replaces the set's.
snapshotAbout: An eye snapshot every 12 s and 4 s into each conversation (tools/conversation-from-save.ps1 -SnapshotEvery), on one contact sheet per run with each snapshot's drawn hands against the controllers (tools/audit-report.py).

canariesAbout: Broken runs the audit must catch (research/69 "Broken runs the audit must catch"; tools/conversation-audit.ps1 -Canaries): each plays a scene of the set, in a game of its own, with a fixed bug brought back by a test switch (`switch`, put back by `restore` after the scene) or without what the audit needs (`hands`: "" replays no hands); caught when any rule of `mustFind` trips (`expect`: one of the scene's expectations failed; `not-measured`: the report says the body was not measured). A broken run the audit passes clean is a blind spot: the run's exit code is 1.
